Feed the red wire 5 V (ESP32 5V/VIN, Pico VBUS); the I2C pull-ups go to the unit's own 3.3 V, so the bus stays 3.3 V-safe.
Counter: write 0x10, read 2 bytes, value = signed(L | H << 8). Write 0x40 = 1 to reset it.
Switch: write 0x20, read 1 byte; 0 means pressed (M5Stack's Arduino example and UIFlow driver), although the protocol PDF says 1 = pressed.
LEDs: write 0x30 then index (0 = both, 1, 2), R, G, B.

driver.code:
# M5Stack Unit Encoder (SKU U135), MicroPython driver.
# An STM32F030F4P6 running M5Stack's firmware counts the knob and reads its push switch.
# I2C address 0x40. Register map (M5Stack Unit Encoder I2C protocol, firmware V1/V1.1):
#   0x00 MODE    (W)   0 = pulse (default), 1 = AB
#   0x10 COUNTER (R/W) signed 16-bit count, low byte first (0x10 = L, 0x11 = H)
#   0x20 SWITCH  (R)   1 byte; reads 0 while the knob is pressed (switch to GND, 10 k pull-up),
#                      as M5Stack's own Arduino example and UIFlow driver use it
#   0x30 RGB     (W)   LED index (0 = both, 1, 2), then R, G, B (0-255 each)
#   0x40 RESET   (W)   write 1 to clear the counter
# Every access: write the register number, then read (or write data after it in the same transfer).

_ADDR = 0x40
_REG_MODE = 0x00
_REG_COUNTER = 0x10
_REG_BUTTON = 0x20
_REG_RGB = 0x30
_REG_RESET = 0x40


class UnitEncoder:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=_ADDR):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        if addr not in i2c.scan():
            raise OSError('Unit Encoder not found at 0x%02x: check the Grove cable and 5 V supply' % addr)

    def _read(self, reg, n):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([reg]))
        return self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, n)

    def _write(self, reg, data):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([reg]) + bytes(data))

    def value(self):
        """Encoder count (signed 16-bit, wraps at +/-32768)."""
        b = self._read(_REG_COUNTER, 2)
        v = b[0] | (b[1] << 8)
        return v - 0x10000 if v & 0x8000 else v

    def set_value(self, v):
        """Write the counter (signed 16-bit)."""
        v &= 0xFFFF
        self._write(_REG_COUNTER, (v & 0xFF, v >> 8))

    def reset(self):
        """Clear the counter to 0."""
        self._write(_REG_RESET, (1,))

    def pressed(self):
        """True while the knob is pushed in (switch register reads 0)."""
        return self._read(_REG_BUTTON, 1)[0] == 0

    def set_mode(self, ab=False):
        """Counting mode: False = pulse (default), True = AB."""
        self._write(_REG_MODE, (1 if ab else 0,))

    def set_led(self, index, r, g, b):
        """Set an RGB LED: index 0 = both, 1 or 2 = one LED; r, g, b 0-255."""
        self._write(_REG_RGB, (index, r & 0xFF, g & 0xFF, b & 0xFF))

# M5Stack Unit Encoder (U135)

## Overview
A rotary encoder knob with a push switch and two SK6812 RGB LEDs, read over I2C. An **STM32F030F4P6** running M5Stack's firmware counts the knob in a signed 16-bit counter, reads the switch and drives the LEDs, so you only need SDA and SCL. An HT7533 regulator makes 3.3 V for the MCU from the 5 V pin; the LEDs run from 5 V.

## Pinout (Grove HY2.0-4P, M5Stack PinMap order)
| Pin | Wire | Function |
|---|---|---|
| GND | Black | Ground |
| 5V | Red | Supply, 5 V |
| SDA | Yellow | I2C data (10 k pull-up to the unit's 3.3 V) |
| SCL | White | I2C clock (10 k pull-up to the unit's 3.3 V) |

## Electrical limits
- Supply: **5 V** (4.5-5.5 V; the SK6812 LEDs need 5 V). About 17 mA with the LEDs off, up to roughly 100 mA more with both LEDs full white.
- The I2C lines are pulled up to the unit's own 3.3 V, so they are safe for 3.3 V boards (ESP32, Pico, Raspberry Pi).

## Interface details (I2C address 0x40)
| Reg | Access | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | W | Mode: 0 = pulse (default), 1 = AB |
| 0x10 | R/W | Counter, signed 16-bit, **low byte first** (0x10 L, 0x11 H) |
| 0x20 | R | Switch: **0 while pressed** (see Gotchas) |
| 0x30 | W | LED index (0 = both, 1, 2), then R, G, B |
| 0x40 | W | Write 1 to reset the counter |

Read: write the register number, then read the bytes. Write: register number followed by the data in one transfer.

## Wiring
| Unit | ESP32 | Raspberry Pi Pico | Raspberry Pi 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| GND (black) | GND | GND | pin 6 |
| 5V (red) | 5V / VIN | VBUS | pin 2 |
| SDA (yellow) | GPIO21 | GP4 | pin 3 |
| SCL (white) | GPIO22 | GP5 | pin 5 |

Use a Grove-to-jumper cable on a breadboard.

## Using the driver
```python
from machine import I2C, Pin
from m5_unit_encoder import UnitEncoder
i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(21), scl=Pin(22))
enc = UnitEncoder(i2c)            # address 0x40
print(enc.value(), enc.pressed())
enc.set_led(0, 0, 40, 0)          # both LEDs dim green
enc.reset()                       # counter back to 0
```

## Gotchas
- **Switch polarity:** M5Stack's protocol PDF says 1 = pressed, but the switch pulls a 10 k pull-up to GND and M5Stack's own Arduino example (`if (!btn_status)`) and UIFlow driver (`not buf[0]`) both treat **0 as pressed**. The driver follows the code. If your firmware is different, flip `pressed()`.
- The counter is 16-bit and wraps at ±32768.
- Needs 5 V: from 3.3 V the LEDs do not light properly.
- In the Sparkbench simulator the slider sets the counter register; LED colours and mode writes are accepted but not shown.

## Datasheet
- Product page / PinMap: https://docs.m5stack.com/en/unit/encoder
- I2C protocol: https://m5stack-doc.oss-cn-shenzhen.aliyuncs.com/801/Unit-Encoder_Protocol.pdf
- Schematic: https://static-cdn.m5stack.com/resource/docs/products/unit/encoder/encoder_sch_01.webp

from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from m5_unit_encoder import UnitEncoder

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
enc = UnitEncoder(i2c)
while True:
    print('count=%d btn=%s' % (enc.value(), 'down' if enc.pressed() else 'up'))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
